plan.title: Database Query CLI (ptbot query)
plan.summary: Add a `ptbot query` subcommand (or thin wrapper) that lets users explore the SQLite deal database from the terminal without needing the Streamlit dashboard or a separate sqlite3 client.
plan.motivation: With the new SQLite persistence layer, users and operators need a quick way to list runs, search deals by target/acquirer/sector, inspect multiples, and export subsets. Currently the only options are the Streamlit dashboard or raw sqlite3. A lightweight CLI query interface makes the DB immediately useful for power users and scripting.
deliverables: Extend src/ptbot/db.py with convenient query helpers: list_runs(), search_deals(filters), get_run_details(), export_deals()
New CLI entry or subcommand (ptbot query runs, ptbot query deals, ptbot query export) with useful flags (--sector, --geography, --since, --format json|table|csv)
Pretty table output using rich or tabulate (or stdlib if we stay minimal)
JSON output mode for scripting and piping into other tools
New tests in tests/test_db.py or a dedicated test_query.py covering the new helpers and CLI surface
constraints: No new runtime dependencies (stay with stdlib + existing pydantic)
Must work when DB does not exist (graceful message)
Must respect --db-path the same way the rest of the tool does
Keep the interface simple; do not duplicate the full power of the Streamlit dashboard
Frozen models — do not change DealCandidate or ResearchParams
